newsitem.title: CHINA: Coke opens 17th China plant as sales boom.
newsitem.headline: Coke opens 17th China plant as sales boom.

text.p: Coca-Cola opened its 17th plant in China Thursday and the head of its China operation said sales should be up 32 percent this year as the brand's popularity continues its phenomenal growth.

John Farrell, head of Coke's China operation, said total Chinese sales of Coca-Cola in 1996 would be an estimated 230-250 million units, equivalent to six billion bottles of Coke, or five for every person in the country.
Annual growth in sales this year should be around 32 percent, compared with 38 percent for 1995, he said.
"The potential numbers are unbelievable," he said.
Coke outsells Pepsi by three-to-one across China.

The new plant, in the central Chinese city of Zhengzhou, will supply Coke to the 90 million people in the province of Henan. The $18 million plant is 70 percent owned by Coke, Hong Kong-based Swire Beverages Ltd. and China International Trust and Investment Corp.
A 24 percent stake is held by a local Zhengzhou state-owned food factory, with the rest held by Beijing Chong Yin Industrial and Trading Co.
Advertising spending to drive recognition of the brand into the minds of China's consumers is nearly doubling each year, but Farrell declined to give any figures.
He said the biggest problem the company faced was finding and training suitable staff quickly enough to keep up with the explosive growth rate.
